lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
A bounce relay lets players carry the ball in their arms to be faster. Which rule keeps the skill practice meaningful and which keeps it safe?

FEEDBACK
Meaningful rule: the ball must bounce at least once every second step. Safe rule: walk or jog, keep lanes separate and wait until the person ahead has finished. The rules protect both the skill and the players.

WATCH FOR
Thinking that bending the rules a little is fine if nobody notices. Fair play means following the rules even when no one is watching, because it keeps the game fair and safe.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Design a striking or bouncing game for two or three players. Write the rules, how to score, two safety rules and a change for a player who cannot stand for long. Play it and note which rule you changed and why.

Write a short reflection naming one choice you changed and why. Any movement is optional, adult-supervised and can be done in a gentler way or described instead.

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
Example game 'Balloon volley': two teams of two keep a balloon above a line of chairs using open hands. Rules: score one point when the balloon lands on the other side; strike with hands only; no running into others. Change for inclusion: players may play seated, or hit the balloon twice.

TRY FIRST
A bounce relay lets players carry the ball in their arms to be faster. Which rule keeps the skill practice meaningful and which keeps it safe?

FEEDBACK
Meaningful rule: the ball must bounce at least once every second step. Safe rule: walk or jog, keep lanes separate and wait until the person ahead has finished. The rules protect both the skill and the players.

Fair play includes agreeing on the rules before starting, taking turns, keeping safe distances from bats or racquets and encouraging everyone. Rules can be changed so that every player can join in.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make safe, healthy and respectful choices using clear cues and reasons, rather than guessing or copying others. Every choice keeps bodies safe and includes everyone.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the cues, rules or choices that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. For any movement, use a clear space, ask an adult to be nearby, move at your own comfortable level and stop if anything hurts or feels unsafe. You may always choose a gentler version or only describe the movement. One deliberate, reasoned change is more useful than a longer answer.
